localBiteReport: The fall transition is underway on Choctawhatchee Bay, and inshore action is picking up as the Destin Fishing Rodeo kicks off in October. Redfish and speckled trout are the headline inshore story right now, with guides reporting them heating up in the bayous and on grass flats as water temperatures moderate; the most recent local report from Half Hitch (dated September 28) is about 19 days old, not this week, so treat it as a recent-but-not-current snapshot. Speckled trout have been fattening up on pinfish across the bay's grass flats, and redfish have been the dominant bay species with flounder gigging also picking up — consistent with the typical early-fall pattern for this area. Water temperature is 81°F. The Destin Fishing Rodeo runs all of October, creating high charter activity across the bay.
